content: Adverse reactions to amoxicillin, similar to other penicillins, are primarily related to hypersensitivity phenomena. These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals with a history of hypersensitivity to penicillins or those with a history of allergies, asthma, hay fever, or urticaria. Reported Adverse Reactions: 1. Infections and Infestations: Mucocutaneous candidiasis has been reported. 2. Gastrointestinal Reactions: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, black hairy tongue, and hemorrhagic or pseudomembranous colitis have been observed. Symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis may manifest during or after antibiotic treatment. (Refer to WARNINGS for further details.) 3. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Anaphylaxis (Refer to WARNINGS). Serum sickness-like reactions, erythematous maculopapular rashes, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hypersensitivity vasculitis, and urticaria have been reported. These hypersensitivity reactions can often be managed with antihistamines and, if necessary, systemic corticosteroids. If such reactions occur, amoxicillin should be discontinued unless the treating physician determines that the condition being treated is life-threatening and can only be managed with amoxicillin therapy. 4. Liver-Related Reactions: Moderate elevations in AST (SGOT) and/or ALT (SGPT) have been noted, though the clinical significance of these findings is unclear. Hepatic dysfunction, including cholestatic jaundice, hepatic cholestasis, and acute cytolytic hepatitis, has been reported. 5. Renal Reactions: Crystalluria has been reported (Refer to OVERDOSAGE for more details). 6. Hemic and Lymphatic System Reactions: Anemia, including hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, thrombocytopenic purpura, eosinophilia, leukopenia, and agranulocytosis have been reported during penicillin therapy. These reactions are typically reversible upon discontinuation of therapy and are believed to be hypersensitivity-related phenomena. 7. Central Nervous System Reactions: Rarely, reversible hyperactivity, agitation, anxiety, insomnia, confusion, convulsions, behavioral changes, and dizziness have been reported. 8. Miscellaneous Reactions: Tooth discoloration (brown, yellow, or gray staining) has been rarely reported, primarily in pediatric patients. In most cases, discoloration was reduced or eliminated with brushing or dental cleaning. Combination Therapy with Clarithromycin and Lansoprazole: Clinical trials involving combination therapy with amoxicillin, clarithromycin, and lansoprazole, or amoxicillin and lansoprazole, did not reveal any adverse reactions unique to these drug combinations. Adverse reactions observed were consistent with those previously reported for amoxicillin, clarithromycin, or lansoprazole. Triple Therapy (Amoxicillin/Clarithromycin/Lansoprazole): The most frequently reported adverse events were diarrhea (7%), headache (6%), and taste perversion (5%). No treatment-emergent adverse events occurred at significantly higher rates with triple therapy compared to any dual therapy regimen. Dual Therapy (Amoxicillin/Lansoprazole): The most frequently reported adverse events were diarrhea (8%) and headache (7%). No treatment-emergent adverse events occurred at significantly higher rates with amoxicillin and lansoprazole dual therapy compared to lansoprazole alone. For additional information on adverse reactions associated with clarithromycin or lansoprazole, refer to their respective package inserts under the ADVERSE REACTIONS section.
